title: Canonical Period Total reporting + optional voucher tips (frontend)

requirements.summary: Ensure all frontend-reported Period Total / primary owed totals use the canonical formula-based value provided by the report, not legacy meter+tips totals.
acceptanceCriteria: In the Daily Report screen, the value labeled "Period Total" is computed using ((credit meter + voucher meter − cash meter) / 2) + credit tips + voucher tips (not meter+tips).
For each day row in the Daily Report, the primary per-day total shown to the user uses the same canonical formula.
Any other UI locations that present a period/daily owed/period total use the same canonical formula (no alternative/legacy computations remain).
The example from the user’s screenshot scenario produces 731.385 (before currency rounding/formatting) when using the provided inputs.

file_operations.description: Change the displayed per-day primary total and the summary "Period Total" to use the report’s canonical total fields (e.g., daily.periodTotal and report.summary.periodTotal) rather than legacy fields like calculatedTotal/totalCalculated; ensure any remaining meter+tips totals are not presented as the primary Period Total.

Audit the daily totals card to ensure any primary owed/period-style total shown is the canonical owed-driver calculation (not meter+tips); keep meter+tips totals clearly labeled as non-Period-Total (e.g., "Grand Total").

requirements.summary: Support voucher tips as optional in import and UI entry/edit flows by defaulting missing tip fields to zero without validation failures.
acceptanceCriteria: Import: if a pickup’s tip amount and/or tip payment method is missing in imported JSON, the import succeeds by defaulting missing tip amount to 0 and using a sensible default tip payment method (so voucher tips are not required).

UI entry/edit: users can select voucher as a tip payment method and enter a tip amount, but the UI does not require voucher tips specifically; saving with no voucher tips results in voucher tip totals of 0 in reports.
When voucher tips are not present, report voucher tip totals display as $0.00 (or equivalent formatting) and do not affect the canonical Period Total calculation beyond adding 0.

file_operations.description: Update import normalization to treat missing tip and/or tipPaymentMethod as optional: default missing tip to 0 and default missing tipPaymentMethod to a sensible value (e.g., the pickup’s meterPaymentMethod, otherwise cash) instead of throwing validation errors.
Ensure the import UI path uses the updated normalization behavior and presents any remaining import errors without implying tips (including voucher tips) are required.

Ensure edit/save validation does not require tip or tip payment method beyond backend requirements: allow empty tip input to be treated as 0 and keep tip payment method selectable (including voucher) without forcing voucher tips.
Confirm the pickup entry form continues to treat tip as optional (empty => 0) and keeps voucher available as a tip payment method without adding any requirement to enter voucher tips.

requirements.summary: Align frontend labeling so the canonical formula-based value is consistently shown as the main Period Total / per-day total, without substituting meter+tips totals.
acceptanceCriteria: Daily Report dialog: the "Period Total" number corresponds to the canonical formula result from the backend, and matches the backend value exactly (subject only to currency formatting/rounding).
Daily Report per-day cards: the primary total shown for the day uses the canonical formula result (and is not the sum of meter+tips unless that happens to match).
If the app still shows meter+tips totals anywhere, it is clearly not presented as the canonical Period Total and does not conflict with the user’s requirement.

file_operations.description: Update labels and displayed values so the canonical total is the primary displayed per-day total and the summary "Period Total"; if legacy totals remain visible, ensure they are clearly labeled as meter+tips (non-Period-Total) to avoid confusion.

Keep the canonical formula utility (computeOwedDriver) as the single source of truth for any client-side owed/period computations used in the UI, and ensure naming/exports make it difficult to accidentally use meter+tips totals as Period Total.
